publication_scope: Sanitized observations, hashes, and public-source references only; no proprietary binary, Ghidra project, disassembly, decompiler output, or machine-specific path.

evidence_classes.native_static: Observed in the locally obtained native boot image; not a live kernel-memory measurement.
evidence_classes.public_source: Read from Apple's exact public xnu-11215.41.3 tag; not independently confirmed in every downstream compiled function.
evidence_classes.source_assisted_inference: A correspondence between observed instructions and public source, with stripped internal symbol names.
evidence_classes.user_space_experiment: Measures an explicitly implemented user-space mechanism; no result is asserted by this manifest.
evidence_classes.simulation: Modeled or replayed behavior; cannot establish physical page reclamation or native-kernel performance.

native_image.origin: Local boot kernelcache, decoded from its local container; no proprietary binary downloaded.
native_image.address_semantics: Image virtual addresses; not measured live KASLR addresses.

candidate_policy.pattern_search_limit: ADRP plus nearby unsigned-offset 64-bit LDR only; not an exhaustive proof of all accesses.

source_attribution.scope: Pending-work, pressure, fragmentation-percentage, locking, and wake-up structure; not a complete native-subsystem reconstruction.

decompilation.accepted_policy_evidence: Bounded 125-instruction disassembly verified against original cache bytes; no code dump published.
decompilation.rejection_reason: Even after Function-body bounding and direct-callee definitions, pseudo-C followed paths outside the body and emitted PIC/branch warnings; completion status alone was insufficient.
decompilation.exported_interface_scope: Pressure observation and waiting, not a demonstrated policy replacement.
decompilation.intermediate_compatibility: Ghidra-specific fileset extraction; REA/LLVM reports a section-offset error on that intermediate, while the original fileset inspection succeeds.

baseline_guards.claim: macOS ARM64 segment capacity defaults to 65536 bytes, with a boot-argument override; this is not a read of the running segment-size variable.
Minor compaction skips a nonempty segment with no empty slot or less than one page of unused space.
Unused space includes holes plus already populated trailing slack; the immediate minor-compaction threshold is one quarter of segment capacity.
Local queueing and opportunistic compaction paths exist independently of treating the global 10% wake threshold as the entire policy.
Minor compaction moves live slots after the first hole, updates mappings, rounds the compacted end to a page, and depopulates the released physical tail.
Removing the last live slot can release resident physical pages before delayed segment cleanup.
Major compaction rejects a pair if both segments are at least 90% full, or the destination is full by bytes or slots.
Major compaction can populate destination pages; donor release alone is not net physical memory saved.
The source includes contention handling, yielding, and bytes-freed-per-microsecond instrumentation; a learned selector using that rate was not established.
The historical thrashing-detector call path is conditionally excluded for macOS ARM64.

local_reproduction.prerequisites: Original local experiment workspace and its scripts, a lawfully obtained local native cache, REA 6.8.0, Ghidra 12.1.4, Java 21, and Python 3.
